event: European Parliament adopts the revised Waste Framework Directive, creating mandatory textile EPR

sourceTitles: Revised Waste Framework Directive enters into force (EU Commission)

implicationForSNS: The legal basis for textile EPR now exists. From this point the direction of travel is fixed: producers will fund textile collection and reuse.

sourceTitles: Revised Waste Framework Directive enters into force (EU Commission)

implicationForSNS: The clock starts. Social-economy enterprises in second-hand textile collection are exempt from EPR obligations and entitled to have their textile waste managed at no cost by producer responsibility organisations.

event: Ireland must transpose the directive into national law

provenance.input: Waste Framework Directive transposition deadline; Ireland circular textiles roadmap
sourceTitles: Ireland National Policy Statement and Roadmap on Circular Textiles (gov.ie)

implicationForSNS: This is the window to shape how Ireland defines a social economy enterprise. An unincorporated initiative may not qualify; a company limited by guarantee or registered charity almost certainly does. This is the strongest commercial argument for incorporating.

event: Textile EPR schemes must be operational across Member States

sourceTitles: Revised Waste Framework Directive enters into force (EU Commission)

implicationForSNS: Producers begin paying eco-modulated fees; the Irish producer responsibility organisation must fund collection, sorting and reuse. An operator already measuring and known to the scheme is in a far stronger position than one appearing in 2028.

event: Micro-enterprise deferral expires (under 10 staff, up to EUR 2M turnover)

sourceTitles: Waste Framework Directive (EU) 2025/1892 textile EPR dates

implicationForSNS: Small producers come fully into scope, widening the base of companies obliged to fund reuse.

event: European Commission review on textile waste prevention, reuse and recycling targets

provenance.input: Directive review clause on textile targets
sourceTitles: Ireland National Policy Statement and Roadmap on Circular Textiles (gov.ie)

implicationForSNS: EU-wide reuse and recycling targets are likely to follow, further raising the value of measured, proven reuse capacity.
